messages:
harry: Heads-up: after bumping OkHttp to 4.10 our Android SDK started hitting sporadic 401s in integration tests. Repro in samples/http2-coalesce.zip.
maya: any quick logs? looks like the pattern we've seen with follow-ups dropping headers.
harry: short snippet: 
```
I/OkHttp: Connection coalesced to example.com:443 (http/2)
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/onboard
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 Unauthorized
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/onboard (followup)
E/Server: request missing Authorization header
```
oscar: Hmm. We used to inject Authorization via an EventListener (token telemetry), not an Interceptor. Coalesced connections + follow-ups may bypass our telemetry mutation.
maya: Right. EventListener is for observability; it doesn't reliably mutate requests for follow-ups. If we rely on it to add headers, clones/followups won't pick them up.
harry: Repro also shows it more on devices with HTTP/2 enabled and when connection coalescing happens (same cert for multiple hosts).
oscar: Proposed fix: move auth insertion into a lightweight Application Interceptor so every attempt gets header deterministically. Also add a defensive step: Authenticator should only trigger one refresh per call and mark requests as already-retried to avoid loops.
maya: Also consider adding an opt-out for connection coalescing in the SDK when pinning/custom trust store is used: OkHttp's ConnectionSpec and ConnectionPool settings can be tuned. But prefer fixing header insertion first.
harry: Agreed. Small patch plan: (1) add AuthInterceptor that fetches token from tokenProvider synchronously/fast-path; (2) ensure any clone() before retry gets a fresh request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", token); (3) add unit test that simulates coalescing/follow-up and asserts header present.
oscar: We'll also add an emulator integration job: pixel-7a:13 with HTTP/2 enabled and coalescing harness. I'll ask @qa-bot to queue it.
qa-bot: Job queued: http2-coalesce-smoke #1287 (pixel-7a:13). ETA ~10m :gear:
maya: One more note: update devex docs: "Where to mutate requests: Interceptor vs EventListener" and add a short migration note for anyone using EventListener to inject headers.
harry: I'll open a small WIP PR with the interceptor + test and tag you both. After CI green, we'll cut a patch and include change in CHANGELOG under java/kotlin sdk fixes.
